# Overview

**Data:** `Survey_data_career_development_23nov.xlsx` (N = 64; CTO = 32, DTE = 10, Impact = 22)

1. Set up: packages, data, output folder
2. Examine data: raw counts, including free text
3. Derive variables: cohort labels, reverse coding, grouped categories for Table 1
4. Descriptive statistics
   - 4.1 Table 1: sociodemographic and career-related characteristics
   - 4.2 Career characteristics by cohort (for the Results text)
   - 4.3 Table 3 and Supplementary Table S3: career development activities
   - 4.4 COM-B statements: overall and by cohort
   - 4.5 Intervention suggestions: Supplementary Table S2 (n (%) helpful, M (SD))
5. Plots
   - 5.1 Figures 4–6 (COM-B, combined) and Supplementary Figures S1–S9 (by cohort)
   - 5.2 Figure 7 (intervention ratings, combined) and Supplementary Figures S10–S12 (by cohort)

All figures are saved to the folder set in `out_dir`.

# 1. Set up

```{r packages}
# install.packages(c("readxl", "dplyr", "tidyr", "forcats", "stringr", "ggplot2", "psych"))
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)    # load dplyr AFTER any other package; do not load plyr (it masks dplyr functions)
library(tidyr)
library(forcats)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)

# Read in data (use the path for the computer you are on - not included here for privacy)
data <- read_excel("enter_pwd_here.xlsx", sheet = 1)

# Folder where all figures are saved
out_dir <- path.expand("~/enter_pwd_here/career_dev_figures")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Helper functions -----------------------------------------------------------
round_up <- function(x) floor(x + 0.5)            # rounds .5 up (R's round() rounds 62.5 to 62)

# n (%) table with whole-number percentages; denominator = non-missing responses
freq_table <- function(x, levels = NULL) {
  x <- if (is.null(levels)) factor(x) else factor(x, levels = levels)
  tab <- table(x)
  data.frame(category = names(tab), n = as.integer(tab),
             pct = round_up(100 * as.integer(tab) / sum(tab)),
             n_pct = paste0(as.integer(tab), " (", round_up(100 * as.integer(tab) / sum(tab)), ")"))
}

# Same, split by cohort (% within each cohort)
freq_by_cohort <- function(df, var, levels = NULL) {
  df %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[var]])) %>%
    mutate(value = if (is.null(levels)) factor(.data[[var]]) else factor(.data[[var]], levels = levels)) %>%
    count(cohort, value, .drop = FALSE) %>%
    group_by(cohort) %>%
    mutate(n_pct = paste0(n, " (", round_up(100 * n / sum(n)), ")")) %>%
    select(-n) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = cohort, values_from = n_pct)
}
```

# 3. Derive variables

## 3.1 Cohort labels

```{r cohort}
# Shorten cohort labels (works whether the data hold the long or short labels)
data <- data %>%
  mutate(cohort = case_when(
    str_detect(cohort, regex("impact", ignore_case = TRUE))                 ~ "Impact",
    str_detect(cohort, regex("doctoral|DTE", ignore_case = TRUE))           ~ "DTE",
    str_detect(cohort, regex("clinical|trial|CTO", ignore_case = TRUE))     ~ "CTO",
    TRUE ~ cohort))
table(data$cohort, useNA = "always")   # should be CTO 32, DTE 10, Impact 22
```

## 3.2 Reverse coding

Three negatively worded COM-B statements are reverse coded so that "agree" always indicates an enabler.

```{r reverse}
lv_agree <- c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neither agree nor disagree",
              "Agree", "Strongly agree")
reverse_agree <- function(x) rev(lv_agree)[match(x, lv_agree)]   # NA stays NA

data <- data %>%
  mutate(social_comp_r        = reverse_agree(social_comp),
         reflec_conseq_down_r = reverse_agree(reflec_conseq_down),
         auto_emotions_r      = reverse_agree(auto_emotions))

# Checks: each pair should be mirror images
table(data$social_comp);        table(data$social_comp_r)
table(data$reflec_conseq_down); table(data$reflec_conseq_down_r)
table(data$auto_emotions);      table(data$auto_emotions_r)
```

## 3.3 Grouped categories for Table 1

Small categories are combined to protect anonymity.

```{r groupings}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    # Gender
    gender_g = case_when(gender == "Woman" ~ "Woman",
                         gender == "Man"   ~ "Man",
                         !is.na(gender)    ~ "Another gender identity or prefer not to say"),
    # Age
    age_g = case_when(str_detect(age, "^25-34") ~ "25–34",
                      str_detect(age, "^35-44") ~ "35–44",
                      str_detect(age, "^45-54") ~ "45–54",
                      str_detect(age, "^55|^65") ~ "55+",
                      str_detect(age, "Prefer")  ~ "Prefer not to say"),
    # Sexual orientation
    sexual_orient_g = case_when(
      str_detect(sexual_orient, "Heterosexual") ~ "Heterosexual or straight",
      str_detect(sexual_orient, "Bisexual|Gay|Lesbian|self-describe") ~ "LGBQ+ (including bisexual, gay or lesbian, and self-described)",
      !is.na(sexual_orient) ~ "Don't know or prefer not to say"),
    # Ethnicity (order of conditions matters)
    ethnicity_g = case_when(
      str_detect(ethnicity, "Prefer not to say|Any other ethnic group") ~ "Prefer not to say",
      str_detect(ethnicity, "African|Carribean|Caribbean|Black")         ~ "Black / Black British",
      str_detect(ethnicity, "Asian|Chinese|Indian|Pakistani|Bangladeshi") ~ "Asian / Asian British (including any other Asian background)",
      # note: "Northern Irish" is in the British option, so match the Irish option exactly
      str_detect(ethnicity, "Any other White") | ethnicity == "Irish"   ~ "White – any other White background (including Irish, European, Australian)",
      str_detect(ethnicity, "^English")                                  ~ "White – English / Welsh / Scottish / Northern Irish / British"),
    # Parental occupation (Social Mobility Commission groupings)
    ses_g = case_when(
      str_detect(ses, "^Modern professional|^Senior, middle")              ~ "Professional",
      str_detect(ses, "^Clerical|^Small bu")                               ~ "Intermediate",
      str_detect(ses, "^Technical|^Route|^Routine|^Semi|^Long-term")       ~ "Lower socio-economic",
      str_detect(ses, "^Other")                                            ~ "Other (e.g., retired, not applicable, don't know)",
      str_detect(ses, "^Prefer")                                           ~ "Prefer not to say"),
    # Time in current role (4-5 years merged into 3-5 years)
    length_g = case_when(
      length_current == "Less than 12 months" ~ "Less than 12 months",
      length_current == "1-2 years"           ~ "1–2 years",
      length_current == "2-3 years"           ~ "2–3 years",
      length_current %in% c("3-4 years", "4-5 years") ~ "3–5 years",
      length_current == "More than 5 years"   ~ "More than 5 years"),
    # Applied for another UCL role?
    applied = !is.na(last_apply) & !str_detect(last_apply, "haven't applied"),
    # Grade of role applied for (only those who applied)
    apply_grade_g = case_when(
      !applied ~ NA_character_,
      last_apply_specifiy == "Grade above" ~ "Grade above",
      last_apply_specifiy == "Same grade"  ~ "Same grade",
      TRUE                                 ~ "Other or not answered"),
    # Faculty (faculties with < 5 participants combined)
    faculty_g = case_when(
      str_detect(ucl_faculty, "Population Health") ~ "Population Health Sciences",
      str_detect(ucl_faculty, "Vice-Provost")      ~ "Vice-Provost offices",
      str_detect(ucl_faculty, "Engineering")       ~ "Engineering Sciences",
      str_detect(ucl_faculty, "Medical Sciences")  ~ "Medical Sciences",
      ucl_faculty == "Prefer not to say"           ~ "Prefer not to say",
      !is.na(ucl_faculty)                          ~ "Other faculties")
  )

# Checks: every grouped variable should have no unexpected NAs
sapply(select(data, gender_g, age_g, sexual_orient_g, ethnicity_g, ses_g, length_g, faculty_g),
       function(x) sum(is.na(x)))
```

## 4.3 Table 3 and Supplementary Table S3: career development activities

Participants could select more than one activity, so each response is split into separate activities.

```{r activities}
activities_long <- data %>%
  select(cohort, activities_develop) %>%
  mutate(id = row_number(),
         activity = str_split(activities_develop, ",(?![^()]*\\))")) %>%   # split on commas outside brackets
  unnest(activity) %>%
  mutate(activity = str_trim(activity))

# Table 3: overall (N = 64), sorted from most to least common
table3 <- activities_long %>%
  count(activity, sort = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(n_pct = paste0(n, " (", round_up(100 * n / nrow(data)), ")"))
table3

# Supplementary Table S3: by cohort (% of each cohort)
cohort_n <- count(data, cohort, name = "cohort_total")
tableS3 <- activities_long %>%
  count(activity, cohort) %>%
  left_join(cohort_n, by = "cohort") %>%
  mutate(n_pct = paste0(n, " (", round_up(100 * n / cohort_total), ")")) %>%
  select(activity, cohort, n_pct) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = cohort, values_from = n_pct, values_fill = "0") %>%
  left_join(select(table3, activity, total = n), by = "activity") %>%
  arrange(desc(total))
tableS3
```

## 4.4 COM-B statements: overall and by cohort

Agree = agree + strongly agree; disagree = disagree + strongly disagree. Reverse-coded items use the `_r` variables.

```{r comb_items}
comb_items <- tribble(
  ~item,                     ~panel,        ~label,
  # Capability
  "psych_know_expect",       "Capability",  "I know what is expected of me in my role at my current grade",
  "psych_know_nextgrade",    "Capability",  "I know what is expected of me to reach the next grade",
  "psych_know_frame",        "Capability",  "I have knowledge on the UCL Career Frameworks",
  "psych_know_aware",        "Capability",  "I am aware of what career development and progression opportunities are relevant to my role",
  "psych_know_develop",      "Capability",  "I know what career development and progression opportunities are available at UCL for my role",
  "psych_skills_require",    "Capability",  "I have the skills required of me to develop in my role",
  "psych_skills_train",      "Capability",  "I have been offered training and opportunities to help support my development in my role",
  "psych_mem_identify",      "Capability",  "I know how to identify what is required to develop in my career",
  "psych_mem_attention",     "Capability",  "I actively pay attention to professional/career development opportunities at UCL",
  "psych_mem_think",         "Capability",  "My professional/career development is something I actively think about",
  "psych_behav_action",      "Capability",  "I have an action plan and keep track of my professional/career development",
  "phys_skills",             "Capability",  "I have the physical ability to develop my career further and any accessibility needs are met",
  # Opportunity
  "phys_enviro_resources",   "Opportunity", "I have the physical resources required to develop my career (such as IT systems/files, access to buildings)",
  "phys_enviro_time",        "Opportunity", "I have sufficient time to engage in activities to support my career development and progression",
  "phys_opp_fair",           "Opportunity", "The opportunities and processes at UCL about the career progression and development of my role are fair and transparent",
  "phys_opp_easy",           "Opportunity", "The opportunities and processes at UCL about the career progression and development of my role are easy to access",
  "phys_beyond",             "Opportunity", "Beyond my current role, I think there are career opportunities for me at UCL",
  "social_share",            "Opportunity", "My colleagues openly discuss and share resources about professional/career development",
  "social_manager",          "Opportunity", "My line manager encourages me to progress and develop in my career",
  "social_comp_r",           "Opportunity", "There is competition and/or tension within my network about career progression and development",
  "social_network_ucl",      "Opportunity", "I have access to a wider UCL network that enables me to develop my career",
  "social_network_ext",      "Opportunity", "I have access to a wider network outside of UCL that enables me to develop my career",
  # Motivation
  "reflec_identity_expect",  "Motivation",  "It is expected of me to develop professionally whilst in my current role",
  "reflec_capab_conf",       "Motivation",  "I am confident that I can progress and develop at UCL",
  "reflec_opt",              "Motivation",  "I am optimistic about my professional development in my current role",
  "reflec_conseq_benefits",  "Motivation",  "There are benefits to progressing and developing in my career at UCL",
  "reflec_conseq_down_r",    "Motivation",  "There are downsides to progressing and developing in my career at UCL",
  "reflec_conseq_outweigh",  "Motivation",  "The benefits of progressing and developing in my career outweigh the downsides at UCL",
  "reflec_intention_focus",  "Motivation",  "Going forward, I intend to focus on my professional/career development",
  "reflec_intention_feed",   "Motivation",  "I actively seek feedback from my colleagues and/or line manager to identify how I can develop in my career",
  "reflect_goals_priority",  "Motivation",  "Career development is a high priority for me",
  "reflec_goals_self",       "Motivation",  "I have set career goals and objectives for myself",
  "reflec_goals_other",      "Motivation",  "Others (e.g., my line manager/professional frameworks) have set career progression and development goals for me",
  "auto_emotions_r",         "Motivation",  "I feel negative emotions about my career development and progression in my role at UCL"
)

# Summary: n (%) agree, neither, disagree for each statement
comb_summary <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    select(all_of(comb_items$item)) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "response") %>%
    filter(!is.na(response)) %>%
    group_by(item) %>%
    summarise(N = n(),
              agree    = sum(response %in% lv_agree[4:5]),
              neither  = sum(response == lv_agree[3]),
              disagree = sum(response %in% lv_agree[1:2]), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(across(c(agree, neither, disagree),
                  ~ paste0(.x, " (", round_up(100 * .x / N), ")"))) %>%
    left_join(comb_items, by = "item") %>%
    select(panel, label, N, agree, neither, disagree) %>%
    arrange(panel, label)
}

comb_summary(data) %>% print(n = Inf, width = Inf)                    # overall (N = 64)
for (coh in c("CTO", "DTE", "Impact")) {                                # by cohort
  cat("\n=====", coh, "=====\n")
  comb_summary(filter(data, cohort == coh)) %>% print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
}
```

## 4.5 Intervention suggestions: Supplementary Table S2

```{r interventions_table}
lv_help <- c("Strongly unhelpful", "Unhelpful", "Neither helpful or unhelpful",
             "Helpful", "Strongly helpful")
help_scores <- setNames(1:5, lv_help)

# Labels include the BCW intervention type
items_help <- c(
  int_aware            = "Awareness and guidance on where to access\ncareer development resources (education)",
  int_career_frame     = "Career framework (education, environmental restructuring)",
  int_train_external   = "More training opportunities (external) (training)",
  int_train_internal   = "More training opportunities (internal) (training)",
  int_secon            = "Programme for external secondments (training, environmental restructuring)",
  int_network_external = "Networking with staff in similar roles outside UCL (enablement)",
  int_cop              = "Community of Practice specific to my role (enablement, environmental restructuring)",
  int_network_ucl      = "Networking with staff in similar roles at UCL (enablement)",
  int_grade_jobs_desc  = "Grade-specific standardised job descriptions (environmental restructuring)",
  int_coach            = "Coaching opportunities (enablement)",
  int_mentor           = "Mentoring opportunities (enablement, environmental restructuring)",
  int_grade_jobs_title = "Grade-specific standardised job titles (environmental restructuring)",
  int_case             = "Case studies of different roles (modelling)"
)

help_long <- data %>%
  select(cohort, all_of(names(items_help))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-cohort, names_to = "item", values_to = "response") %>%
  filter(!is.na(response)) %>%
  mutate(score = help_scores[response],
         helpful = response %in% lv_help[4:5])

# Overall: n (%) helpful and M (SD)
help_overall <- help_long %>%
  group_by(item) %>%
  summarise(helpful_n_pct = paste0(sum(helpful), " (", round_up(100 * mean(helpful)), ")"),
            pct_helpful   = 100 * mean(helpful),
            M_SD          = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(score), sd(score)), .groups = "drop")

# By cohort: % helpful and M (SD)
help_cohort <- help_long %>%
  group_by(item, cohort) %>%
  summarise(value = paste0(round_up(100 * mean(helpful)), "% | ",
                           sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(score), sd(score))), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = cohort, values_from = value)

tableS2 <- help_overall %>%
  left_join(help_cohort, by = "item") %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_helpful)) %>%
  mutate(item = str_replace_all(items_help[item], "\n", " ")) %>%
  select(-pct_helpful)
tableS2 %>% print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

# 5. Plots

## 5.1 Figures 4–6 (COM-B, combined) and Supplementary Figures S1–S9 (by cohort)

```{r comb_plots}
comb_cols <- setNames(c("#b2182b", "#ef8a62", "#cccccc", "#67a9cf", "#2166ac"), lv_agree)

plot_comb <- function(df, which_panel, wrap = 55) {
  n_resp <- nrow(df)
  it <- filter(comb_items, panel == which_panel)

  plot_df <- df %>%
    select(all_of(it$item)) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "response") %>%
    filter(!is.na(response)) %>%
    left_join(it, by = "item") %>%
    mutate(response = factor(response, levels = lv_agree)) %>%
    count(item, label, response) %>%
    complete(nesting(item, label), response, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
    arrange(item, response) %>%
    group_by(item) %>%
    mutate(pct     = 100 * n / sum(n),
           offset  = -(sum(pct[response %in% lv_agree[1:2]]) + pct[response == lv_agree[3]] / 2),
           xmax    = offset + cumsum(pct),
           xmin    = xmax - pct,
           barrier = sum(pct[response %in% lv_agree[1:2]])) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(label_w = str_wrap(label, wrap),
           label_f = fct_reorder(label_w, -barrier),             # largest barriers at the top
           y       = length(unique(label_w)) + 1 - as.numeric(label_f))

  ggplot(plot_df) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = y - 0.36, ymax = y + 0.36, fill = response),
              colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(data = filter(plot_df, pct >= 6),
              aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = y, label = round_up(pct),
                  colour = response %in% c(lv_agree[1], lv_agree[5])), size = 2.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey15"), guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = comb_cols, breaks = lv_agree, labels = lv_agree, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = distinct(plot_df, y, label_w)$y,
                       labels = distinct(plot_df, y, label_w)$label_w,
                       expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-100, 100, 25), labels = abs(seq(-100, 100, 25))) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-100, 100)) +                       # never drops long bars
    labs(x = paste0("Percentage of respondents (N = ", n_resp, ")"), y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(panel.grid      = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y     = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey10", lineheight = 0.95),
          axis.line.x     = element_line(colour = "grey30"),
          axis.ticks.x    = element_line(colour = "grey30"),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"),
          legend.text     = element_text(size = 7),
          plot.margin     = margin(5, 10, 5, 5)) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))
}

save_tiff <- function(p, file, height_cm) {
  ggsave(file.path(out_dir, file), p, width = 17, height = height_cm, units = "cm",
         dpi = 600, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
}

panels <- c(Capability = 4, Opportunity = 5, Motivation = 6)   # main-text figure numbers

# Main text: Figures 4-6 (combined)
for (pn in names(panels)) {
  h <- 3 + 1.25 * sum(comb_items$panel == pn)
  save_tiff(plot_comb(data, pn), paste0("Figure", panels[pn], "_COMB_", pn, "_combined.tiff"), h)
}

# Supplementary: S1-S9 (S1-S3 capability, S4-S6 opportunity, S7-S9 motivation; CTO, DTE, Impact)
s <- 1
for (pn in names(panels)) {
  h <- 3 + 1.25 * sum(comb_items$panel == pn)
  for (coh in c("CTO", "DTE", "Impact")) {
    save_tiff(plot_comb(filter(data, cohort == coh), pn),
              paste0("Supp_FigureS", s, "_COMB_", pn, "_", coh, ".tiff"), h)
    s <- s + 1
  }
}

plot_comb(data, "Opportunity")   # preview one in RStudio
```

## 5.2 Figure 7 (intervention ratings, combined) and Supplementary Figures S10–S12 (by cohort)

```{r help_plots}
help_cols   <- setNames(c("#b2182b", "#ef8a62", "#cccccc", "#67a9cf", "#2166ac"), lv_help)
help_legend <- c("Strongly unhelpful", "Unhelpful", "Neither helpful nor unhelpful",
                 "Helpful", "Strongly helpful")

plot_helpfulness <- function(df) {
  n_resp <- nrow(df)

  plot_df <- df %>%
    select(all_of(names(items_help))) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "response") %>%
    filter(!is.na(response)) %>%
    mutate(response = factor(response, levels = lv_help)) %>%
    count(item, response) %>%
    complete(item, response, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
    arrange(item, response) %>%
    group_by(item) %>%
    mutate(pct     = 100 * n / sum(n),
           offset  = -(sum(pct[response %in% lv_help[1:2]]) + pct[response == lv_help[3]] / 2),
           xmax    = offset + cumsum(pct),
           xmin    = xmax - pct,
           helpful = sum(pct[response %in% lv_help[4:5]])) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(label = fct_reorder(unname(items_help[item]), helpful),   # ordered by % helpful
           y     = as.numeric(label))

  ggplot(plot_df) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = y - 0.36, ymax = y + 0.36, fill = response),
              colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(data = filter(plot_df, pct >= 6),
              aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = y, label = round_up(pct),
                  colour = response %in% c(lv_help[1], lv_help[5])), size = 2.4) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey15"), guide = "none") +
    geom_text(data = distinct(plot_df, y, helpful),
              aes(x = 103, y = y, label = paste0(round_up(helpful), "%")),
              hjust = 0, fontface = "bold", colour = "#2166ac", size = 2.5) +
    annotate("text", x = 103, y = max(plot_df$y) + 0.9, label = "Helpful\n(total)",
             hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = 2.3, lineheight = 0.9, colour = "#2166ac") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = help_cols, breaks = lv_help, labels = help_legend, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_along(levels(plot_df$label)), labels = levels(plot_df$label),
                       expand = expansion(add = c(0.6, 1.8))) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-40, 100, 20), labels = abs(seq(-40, 100, 20))) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-45, 115)) +
    labs(x = paste0("Percentage of respondents (N = ", n_resp, ")"), y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
    theme(panel.grid      = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y     = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey10", lineheight = 0.9),
          axis.line.x     = element_line(colour = "grey30"),
          axis.ticks.x    = element_line(colour = "grey30"),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"),
          legend.text     = element_text(size = 6.5),
          plot.margin     = margin(5, 10, 5, 5)) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))
}

# Main text: Figure 7 (combined)
save_tiff(plot_helpfulness(data), "Figure7_intervention_ratings_combined.tiff", 13)

# Supplementary: S10-S12 (CTO, DTE, Impact)
s <- 10
for (coh in c("CTO", "DTE", "Impact")) {
  save_tiff(plot_helpfulness(filter(data, cohort == coh)),
            paste0("Supp_FigureS", s, "_intervention_ratings_", coh, ".tiff"), 13)
  s <- s + 1
}

plot_helpfulness(data)   # preview in RStudio

# Check all 16 figures were saved
list.files(out_dir)
```
